Subject: Re: kurila 1.3 released

* Rafael Garcia-Suarez  [2007-10-11 19:35]:
> Now if I can say what I think, as a Perl 5 pumpking: Kurila
> takes the problem by the wrong end: that is, by Perl 5's
> codebase. Basically, what's wrong with Perl 5 is its lack of
> extensibility.
> 
> To solve the lack of extensibility problem, a
> re-orthogonalisation of the syntax is needed. Removing bits of
> syntax will not help with the fact that prototypes are a
> nightmare, that exceptions are badly integrated, that runtime
> type checking via can() or ref() is broken, that qr// is
> implemented in a cumbersome way, that the implementation of
> magic is riddled with special cases. Those things need a
> complete rethinking. Hence Perl 6. The Perl 6 effort is driven
> by language design and syntax changes. Kurila (read the last
> announcement) is driven by internal refactoring and juggling.

I hate to bring it up, and I’m not particularly fond of dumping
on Perl 6, but compare how that effort is going with the Python
3000 track record, which took the “internal refactoring and
juggling (and it’s OK to break backcompat)” approach vs. the
“complete retink” approach of Perl 6.

I dunno.

If Gerard has the energy to pursue kurila on his own, I say he
should.

I also agree that p5p is probably not the place to discuss it –
not forever, anyway. However, I think for the time being it might
be better to keep that discussion here; I was recently reading a
bunch of Linus Torvalds lkml posts about Con Kolivas’ patches,
and somewhere he makes the point that special-interest mailing
list like the -ck patchset ML are problematic because they become
an echo chamber with no cross-polination of ideas and viewpoints.
That rings completely true.

Regards,
-- 
Aristotle Pagaltzis //
